title: Tensor coherence of the normalized integral quotient pullback square
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ put $R_T=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}(A/\pi^m)_T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], and $S_T=(A/\pi^n)_T$, the constant finite quotient ring sheaf, for a fixed $n\geq1$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D_R(T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T})$, $D_S(T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{S_T})$ of internal module objects, the derived module pullback and pushforward with their derived adjunction [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and the uncompleted relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Set $D_{n,T}K=K\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$, the derived scalar extension of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

For any scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, write $D_T=D_{n,T}$, $L_R=L_{f,R}$ and $L_S=L_{f,S}$. Let $\lambda:L_SD_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}D_XL_R$ be precisely the normalized comparison of [lem-sfb-integral-quotient-direct-image-comparison]. Use the actual internal pullback tensor maps $t_R,t_S$ of [def-sfb-module-object-projection-map] and the normalized scalar tensor isomorphisms $b_T$ characterized by [lem-sfb-quotient-section-tensor-normalization].

Consider the square of ringed topoi with horizontal morphisms induced by $f$ and vertical morphisms $(T,S_T)\to(T,R_T)$ induced by the identity topos and the actual quotient $R_T\to S_T$. Its two composite structural ring maps agree under the canonical inverse-image compositor. More precisely, the coefficient identifications $\alpha_f$ for $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and $A/\pi^n$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] intertwine the actual quotient ring maps. The comparison $\lambda$ is identified, under the internal/section equivalences, with the composition comparison between the two routes around this square, with its stated flat-term K-flat normalization.

For every $U,V\in D_R(Y)$, the following equality holds in $D_S(X)$:
$$b_{X,L_RU,L_RV}\circ D_X(t_{R,U,V})\circ\lambda_{U\otimes^L_{R_Y}V}
=(\lambda_U\otimes^L_{S_X}\lambda_V)\circ t_{S,D_YU,D_YV}\circ L_S(b_{Y,U,V}).$$
Both sides have source $L_SD_Y(U\otimes^L_{R_Y}V)$ and target $D_XL_RU\otimes^L_{S_X}D_XL_RV$. Thus the two composite tensorators $t_S\circ L_S(b_Y)$ and $b_X\circ D_X(t_R)$ are intertwined by this specified $\lambda$, naturally in $U,V$. No interchange of the two homogeneous module variables occurs in these comparisons. The assertion holds for arbitrary unbounded complexes and for nonflat quotient maps; it assumes neither properness nor completeness.

proof.text:
Write $q:\underline A\to\underline{A/\pi^n}$ for the actual condensed quotient, and $q_T:R_T\to S_T$ for its pullback. These are precisely the maps defined in [def-sfb-integral-quotient-coefficients], with its zero-based index $n-1$. By [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], $\alpha_{f,R}$ and $\alpha_{f,S}$ are components of the same natural isomorphism $f^{-1}p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$. Naturality at $q$ gives
$$\alpha_{f,S}\circ f^{-1}(q_Y)=q_X\circ\alpha_{f,R}.$$
Thus the paths $(X,S_X)\to(Y,S_Y)\to(Y,R_Y)$ and $(X,S_X)\to(X,R_X)\to(Y,R_Y)$ have the same structural ring map after the canonical inverse-image compositor. This establishes commutation of the actual ringed square, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between its corner rings.

proof.text: Apply quotient_section_tensor_normalization to the given normalized tensor isomorphisms. Its ComparisonSpec supplies one family c of normalized scalar section data and, for f and the given normalized lam, a section comparison barLam satisfying both PullSectionCondition and SectionPullNormalized. Take c(X), c(Y) and that barLam. This proves the entire second conjunct without reconstructing a separate ringed composition comparison.

For flat-term K-flat complexes P and Q in the internal source module category, apply the representative tensor calculation of [lem-sfb-quotient-pullback-tensor-flat-model]. This gives precisely the last conjunct on the pair (Q(P),Q(Q)); its proof is the ordinary balancing calculation and signed-total argument.

Regard the left and right composites in the tensor equation as natural transformations between functors on D_R(Y) times D_R(Y). For arbitrary U,V, take preimage complexes under the derived localization and apply CochainComplex.exists_quasiIso_flat_kFlat from [lem-sfb-abstract-kflat-resolution]. Their quasi-isomorphisms yield isomorphisms eP:Q(P) to U and eQ:Q(Q) to V. Naturality rewrites each transformation at (U,V), after precomposition by the source functor image of (eP,eQ), as its value at (Q(P),Q(Q)) followed by the target functor image. The representative equality of step 3 equates these expressions. Cancel the source image, which is an isomorphism, to get equality at (U,V). This is implemented by the proved private lemma natTrans_ext_flat. No two-variable localization or site descent theorem is required.
